modelResponse.episodeSummary: George F. Antonelli, Sinus Bradycardia, Warning, Hemodynamically stable (BP 108/64)
keyECGEvidence: Sinus P waves with prolonged PR
modelResponse.mechanism: Pharmacokinetic interaction where amiodarone inhibited the renal/p-glycoprotein clearance of digoxin, leading to supratherapeutic serum levels (digoxin 2.4 ng/mL TOXIC) and symptomatic bradycardia.

rejectedAlternatives.why: While amiodarone contributes to bradycardia, the presence of 'Scooped/sagging ST segments', 'U waves', and a 'digoxin 2.4 ng/mL TOXIC' level specifically identifies digoxin toxicity as the driver of the current clinical state and nausea.
K 4.0 mmol/L is within normal limits; U waves are present but potassium is not low.

recommendedActions: Order Digoxin-specific antibody fragments (DigiFab/Digibind) if clinical status worsens or bradycardia persists
Monitor serum electrolytes (especially K+) and renal function
Hold Warfarin and monitor INR (due to amiodarone interaction)
Hold Simvastatin (due to amiodarone interaction/risk of myopathy given CK 1200 U/L HIGH)
